status: Isolated source proposal. NOT installed or selected by production native registration.
moduleContract: Both modules declare exactly22 pinned Node22 ESM exports. node:assert default===ok; named strict===node:assert/strict default; strict.strict===strict; strict.ok===root.ok. Strict equal/notEqual/deepEqual/notDeepEqual alias the root strict variants. Functions on each default initially share identity with named exports; later default-property reassignment does not rewrite named ESM cells. Future selected literal CommonJS lowering may return default; runtime require and syncBuiltinESMExports are excluded.

node:assert.callablePolicy: Deferred functions synchronously throw TypeError ERR_SM_NODE_UNSUPPORTED with operation on call and construction, including application initialization. Supported throws/doesNotThrow execute the callback before applicable matcher handling. A successful doesNotThrow returns without consulting an unused matcher.
deviations: Auto messages use bounded opaque-object rendering, without util.inspect, custom inspectors, V8 source-file expression lookup, rich diffs, color or exact Node stack framing. Successful assertions do not render diagnostic inputs.

AssertionError preserves tested code/name/operator/generatedMessage and actual/expected identity. stackStartFn/stackStartFunction are ignored; details is explicitly deferred. Native error stack layout, custom message diff decoration and prototype inspection helpers differ.

Ordinary same-realm Error messages are rethrown by identity for ok/equality/fail/match; throws matcher failure renders its supplied message, matching the pinned reference. Cross-realm native-error detection and proxies posing as errors/regexps are not claimed.
Complex exception validation objects and Error-instance matchers are deferred. Error constructors/classes, ordinary predicates returning exactly true and native RegExp matching are supported.
RegExp matching uses captured native exec and retains lastIndex behavior; regex algorithmic complexity remains the JavaScript engine's responsibility.
Async helpers are synchronous explicit unsupported operations rather than partial Promise implementations. No async scheduling or AsyncLocalStorage behavior is claimed.
Warning delivery for deprecated fail overload and CallTracker is deferred. No process/stdio/clock/random/filesystem capability is introduced.
Support is not complete Node Assert compatibility or a prerequisite proven by readable-stream4.7: that package uses a private local assertion helper.

node:assert/strict.callablePolicy: Shares the root implementation, references and deferred-operation policy. The four strict aliases do not wrap or duplicate functions.
